name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH19_MCQ_Q01 - Nitrogenous wastes and animal excretory organs

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding nitrogenous wastes and excretory structures across the animal kingdom:

Statement I: Ammonia is the most toxic nitrogenous waste and is generally excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or gill surfaces as ammonium ions without significant kidney involvement.

Statement II: Mammals, many terrestrial amphibians, and marine fishes are ureotelic animals that convert ammonia into urea in the liver before its excretion by the kidneys.

Statement III: Protonephridia (flame cells) in Platyhelminthes and Amphioxus are primarily concerned with osmoregulation, whereas Malpighian tubules in insects help in both nitrogenous waste removal and osmoregulation.

Statement IV: Antennal glands or green glands are the characteristic excretory structures of earthworms and other annelids.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animals excrete ammonia, urea, or uric acid depending on water availability, using specialized excretory structures ranging from simple tubular forms in invertebrates to kidneys in vertebrates.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ammonotelism
Ammonia is the most toxic nitrogenous waste and is readily soluble in water. In ammonotelic animals (such as bony fishes, aquatic amphibians, and aquatic insects), it is excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or through gill surfaces as ammonium ions, and kidneys do not play any significant role in its removal. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Ureotelism
Mammals, many terrestrial amphibians, and marine fishes mainly excrete urea (ureotelic). Ammonia produced by metabolism is converted into urea in the liver, released into the blood, and filtered and excreted by the kidneys. This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Protonephridia and Malpighian Tubules
Protonephridia or flame cells occur in Platyhelminthes (e.g., Planaria), rotifers, some annelids, and the cephalochordate Amphioxus, functioning primarily in ionic and fluid volume regulation (osmoregulation). Malpighian tubules occur in most insects (including cockroaches) and assist in both nitrogenous waste removal and osmoregulation. This proposition is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Antennal/Green Glands vs Nephridia
Antennal glands or green glands perform the excretory function in crustaceans such as prawns, whereas earthworms and other annelids possess nephridia. Therefore, attributing green glands to earthworms and annelids is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Only the first three propositions regarding ammonotelism, ureotelism, and protonephridia/Malpighian tubules are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH19_MCQ_Q02 - Anatomy and internal organization of human kidneys

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements about the human excretory system and kidney anatomy:

Statement I: Human kidneys are situated between the levels of the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebra close to the dorsal inner wall of the abdominal cavity.

Statement II: Each adult human kidney measures 10–12 cm in length, 5–7 cm in width, and 2–3 cm in thickness, with an average weight of 120–170 g.

Statement III: The renal pelvis is a broad funnel-shaped space located outer to the tough renal capsule, and it receives urine directly from the afferent arterioles.

Statement IV: Inside the kidney, the outer cortex extends in between the conical medullary pyramids as renal columns called Columns of Bertini.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human kidney has a defined retroperitoneal position, characteristic adult dimensions, and an internal organization divided into an outer cortex and inner medulla.

Step 2: Evaluation of Anatomical Position
Human kidneys are reddish-brown, bean-shaped organs located close to the dorsal inner wall of the abdominal cavity between the levels of the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebra. This is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Kidney Dimensions and Weight
An adult human kidney measures 10–12 cm in length, 5–7 cm in width, 2–3 cm in thickness, and has an average weight of 120–170 g. This is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Renal Pelvis Location and Function
The outer layer of the kidney is a tough capsule. Inner to the hilum (a notch on the inner concave surface) lies the broad funnel-shaped renal pelvis with projections called calyces, which collect urine from collecting ducts via medullary pyramids—not from afferent arterioles. Hence, placing the renal pelvis outer to the capsule and linking it to afferent arterioles is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of Columns of Bertini
The medulla is divided into conical medullary pyramids projecting into the calyces, while the cortex extends between the medullary pyramids as renal columns known as Columns of Bertini. This is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The propositions concerning kidney position, dimensions/weight, and Columns of Bertini are correct, while the claim regarding the renal pelvis is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH19_MCQ_Q03 - Nephron organization and glomerular ultrafiltration

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding nephron structure and glomerular filtration:

Statement I: The glomerulus is a tuft of capillaries formed by the afferent arteriole, and together with the double-walled Bowman's capsule, it forms the Malpighian body or renal corpuscle.

Statement II: In cortical nephrons, the loop of Henle is very short and extends only slightly into the medulla, and the vasa recta is absent or highly reduced.

Statement III: Blood filtration in the glomerulus occurs across three layers: capillary endothelium, basement membrane, and podocytes of Bowman's capsule, allowing plasma proteins to pass freely into the filtrate.

Statement IV: In a healthy individual, the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is approximately \(125\,\mathrm{ml/minute}\), which corresponds to about \(180\,\mathrm{litres}\) per day.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney, where ultrafiltration across the Malpighian body initiates urine formation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Malpighian Body
Afferent arterioles form the glomerular capillary tuft, which is enclosed by the double-walled cup-like Bowman's capsule. Together, the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule constitute the Malpighian body (renal corpuscle). This is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Cortical Nephrons
In the majority of nephrons (cortical nephrons), the loop of Henle is too short and extends only very little into the medulla, and the vasa recta is absent or highly reduced. This is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Ultrafiltration Selectivity
Although glomerular filtration occurs across three layers (glomerular endothelium, basement membrane, and podocytes with filtration slits), blood is filtered so finely that almost all plasma constituents except proteins pass into the lumen of Bowman's capsule. Claiming that plasma proteins pass freely into the filtrate is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of GFR Value
The amount of filtrate formed per minute (GFR) in a healthy individual is approximately \(125\,\mathrm{ml/min}\). Over 24 hours (\(1440\,\mathrm{min}\)), \(125\,\mathrm{ml/min} \times 1440\,\mathrm{min} = 180{,}000\,\mathrm{ml} = 180\,\mathrm{litres/day}\). This is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The propositions regarding the Malpighian body, cortical nephrons, and GFR are correct, whereas the claim that plasma proteins pass into the filtrate is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH19_MCQ_Q04 - Tubular reabsorption, secretion, and segment functions

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding tubular reabsorption, secretion, and functions of nephron segments:

Statement I: Nearly 99 per cent of the glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed by the renal tubules, with glucose, amino acids, and \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) reabsorbed actively and nitrogenous wastes absorbed passively.

Statement II: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium and reabsorbs nearly all essential nutrients and 70–80 per cent of electrolytes and water.

Statement III: The descending limb of Henle's loop is permeable to water and almost impermeable to electrolytes, whereas the ascending limb is impermeable to water and allows electrolyte transport.

Statement IV: Tubular cells secrete \(\mathrm{H}^+\), \(\mathrm{K}^+\), and ammonia into the filtrate, which helps maintain the ionic and acid-base balance of body fluids.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
After glomerular filtration, the renal tubules modify the filtrate through selective active and passive reabsorption and tubular secretion.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reabsorption Magnitude and Mechanisms
Comparing 180 litres of daily filtrate to 1.5 litres of urine shows that nearly 99% of the filtrate is reabsorbed. Glucose, amino acids, and \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) are reabsorbed actively, while nitrogenous wastes are absorbed passively. This is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of PCT Structure and Capacity
PCT has a simple cuboidal brush border epithelium that increases absorptive surface area, enabling reabsorption of nearly all essential nutrients and 70–80% of electrolytes and water. This is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Henle's Loop Permeabilities
The descending limb of Henle's loop is permeable to water and nearly impermeable to electrolytes (concentrating the descending filtrate), whereas the ascending limb is impermeable to water and transports electrolytes actively or passively (diluting the ascending filtrate). This is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Tubular Secretion
Tubular cells selectively secrete \(\mathrm{H}^+\), \(\mathrm{K}^+\), and ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH}_3\)) into the filtrate to maintain ionic and acid-base (pH) balance of body fluids. This is also correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
All four physiological propositions regarding reabsorption, PCT function, Henle's loop differential permeability, and tubular secretion are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH19_MCQ_Q05 - DCT, collecting duct, micturition, and urine properties

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding the distal nephron segments and micturition:

Statement I: Conditional reabsorption of \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) and water, reabsorption of \(\mathrm{HCO}_3^-\), and selective secretion of \(\mathrm{H}^+\), \(\mathrm{K}^+\), and \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) occur in the distal convoluted tubule (DCT).

Statement II: The collecting duct allows passage of small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium to help maintain medullary osmolarity.

Statement III: During the micturition reflex, motor signals from the CNS cause relaxation of the smooth muscles of the urinary bladder and contraction of the urethral sphincter.

Statement IV: An adult human excretes on an average 1 to 1.5 litres of slightly acidic urine (pH 6.0) containing 25–30 g of urea per day, and glycosuria and ketonuria are indicative of diabetes mellitus.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The DCT and collecting duct finalize urine composition and osmolarity, after which urine is stored in the bladder and voided via the micturition reflex.

Step 2: Evaluation of DCT Activity
The DCT performs conditional reabsorption of \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) and water, reabsorbs \(\mathrm{HCO}_3^-\), and selectively secretes \(\mathrm{H}^+\), \(\mathrm{K}^+\), and \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) to maintain blood pH and sodium-potassium balance. This is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Collecting Duct Urea Transport
The collecting duct permits passage of small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium to maintain the high osmotic gradient needed for water reabsorption. This is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Micturition Reflex Mechanics
In response to bladder stretch signals, the CNS sends motor messages that initiate contraction of the smooth muscles of the bladder and simultaneous relaxation of the urethral sphincter to release urine. Reversing these muscular actions (claiming bladder relaxation and sphincter contraction) is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of Urine Characteristics
Normal adult urine output is 1–1.5 litres/day, slightly acidic (pH 6.0), with 25–30 g of urea excreted daily. Presence of glucose (glycosuria) and ketone bodies (ketonuria) indicates diabetes mellitus. This is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The descriptions of DCT function, collecting duct urea passage, and urine characteristics/clinical indicators are correct, whereas the description of muscular events during micturition is reversed and incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH19_MCQ_Q06 - Accessory excretory organs and renal disorders

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding accessory excretory organs and disorders of the excretory system:

Statement I: The lungs remove approximately \(200\,\mathrm{mL/minute}\) of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and significant quantities of water every day.

Statement II: The liver secretes bile containing bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins, and drugs, most of which pass out with digestive wastes.

Statement III: Sweat glands eliminate \(\mathrm{NaCl}\), small amounts of urea, and lactic acid, while sebaceous glands eliminate sterols, hydrocarbons, and waxes through sebum.

Statement IV: During hemodialysis, the dialysing fluid contains the same composition as plasma except nitrogenous wastes, allowing wastes to move out of blood across the porous cellophane membrane along a concentration gradient.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Accessory organs (lungs, liver, skin) complement renal excretion, and artificial kidney (hemodialysis) removes accumulated nitrogenous wastes in uremic patients.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pulmonary Excretion
Human lungs eliminate roughly \(200\,\mathrm{mL/minute}\) of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) along with substantial water vapour daily. This is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Hepatic Excretion
The liver secretes bile containing bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins, and drugs, most of which are excreted along with digestive wastes. This is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Cutaneous Excretion
Sweat glands secrete a watery fluid containing \(\mathrm{NaCl}\), small amounts of urea, and lactic acid, whereas sebaceous glands eliminate sterols, hydrocarbons, and waxes through sebum to form a protective oily skin covering. This is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Hemodialysis Principle
In hemodialysis, the dialysing fluid matches blood plasma composition except for the absence of nitrogenous wastes. Consequently, nitrogenous wastes diffuse freely out of the blood across the porous cellophane tube down their concentration gradient. This is also correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
All four propositions covering pulmonary excretion, hepatic bile excretion, sweat/sebaceous gland secretions, and hemodialysis are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH19_MCQ_Q07 - Counter current mechanism and medullary gradient

questiontext.text:
Analyze the following four statements regarding the counter current mechanism for concentrating urine:

Statement I: The flow of filtrate in the two limbs of Henle's loop is in opposite directions, and the flow of blood in the two limbs of the vasa recta is also in a counter current pattern.

Statement II: The osmolarity of the medullary interstitium increases from \(300\,\mathrm{mOsmol\,L}^{-1}\) in the cortex to about \(1200\,\mathrm{mOsmol\,L}^{-1}\) in the inner medulla, mainly due to \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) and urea.

Statement III: \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) transported by the ascending limb of Henle's loop is exchanged with the descending limb of the vasa recta and is returned to the interstitium by the ascending portion of the vasa recta.

Statement IV: Human kidneys can concentrate urine up to nearly ten times that of the initial glomerular filtrate formed in Bowman's capsule.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The counter current multiplier (Henle's loop) and counter current exchanger (vasa recta) establish and preserve a hyperosmotic medullary interstitium that drives water reabsorption from the collecting duct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Counter Current Flow
Filtrate flows in opposite directions in the descending and ascending limbs of Henle's loop, and blood flows in opposite directions in the two limbs of the vasa recta. This is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Osmolarity Gradient and Solutes
Interstitial osmolarity rises from \(300\,\mathrm{mOsmol\,L}^{-1}\) in the cortex to about \(1200\,\mathrm{mOsmol\,L}^{-1}\) in the inner medulla, a gradient primarily maintained by \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) and urea. This is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of NaCl Exchange in Vasa Recta
\(\mathrm{NaCl}\) leaving the ascending limb of Henle's loop enters the descending limb of the vasa recta and is returned to the medullary interstitium by the ascending limb of the vasa recta, preventing solute washout. This is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Concentration Factor
Because the initial filtrate is \(\sim 300\,\mathrm{mOsmol\,L}^{-1}\) and the inner medulla reaches \(\sim 1200\,\mathrm{mOsmol\,L}^{-1}\), human kidneys concentrate urine by a factor of \(\frac{1200}{300} = 4\), i.e., nearly four times—not ten times—the initial filtrate concentration. Thus, claiming a ten-fold concentration is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Only the first three propositions regarding counter current flow, the \(300\)–\(1200\,\mathrm{mOsmol\,L}^{-1}\) gradient, and \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) exchange are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH19_MCQ_Q08 - Hormonal regulation via ADH, RAAS, and ANF

questiontext.text:
Analyze the following four statements regarding hormonal regulation of kidney function:

Statement I: Excessive fluid loss activates osmoreceptors that stimulate the hypothalamus to release ADH (vasopressin) from the neurohypophysis, facilitating water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule.

Statement II: ADH can also constrict blood vessels, thereby increasing blood pressure, glomerular blood flow, and GFR.

Statement III: A fall in GFR activates JG cells to release renin, which converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I and then to angiotensin II; angiotensin II acts as a vasoconstrictor and stimulates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone.

Statement IV: An increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart stimulates the release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF), which causes vasoconstriction and enhances the renin-angiotensin mechanism.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Kidney function and blood pressure are tightly regulated by hormonal feedback involving the hypothalamus/neurohypophysis (ADH), the juxtaglomerular apparatus (Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone), and the heart (ANF).

Step 2: Evaluation of ADH Osmoregulatory Role
Excessive fluid loss activates osmoreceptors, prompting the hypothalamus to release ADH from the neurohypophysis. ADH promotes water reabsorption in the latter parts of the tubule, preventing diuresis. This is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of ADH Vascular Action
Beyond tubular water reabsorption, ADH exerts constrictory effects on blood vessels, raising blood pressure and consequently increasing glomerular blood flow and GFR. This is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone Pathway
When glomerular blood flow/pressure/GFR falls, JG cells release renin, converting angiotensinogen to angiotensin I and further to angiotensin II. Angiotensin II is a potent vasoconstrictor that increases glomerular blood pressure and also activates the adrenal cortex to secrete aldosterone, which promotes \(\mathrm{Na}^+\) and water reabsorption from the distal tubule. This is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of ANF Action
Increased blood flow to the cardiac atria triggers ANF release, which causes vasodilation (not vasoconstriction), lowers blood pressure, and acts as a check (inhibitory counterbalance)—not an enhancer—on the renin-angiotensin mechanism. Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The first three propositions describing ADH actions and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone cascade are correct, whereas the claim that ANF causes vasoconstriction and enhances the renin-angiotensin mechanism is incorrect.
